data.text: Luke, I learned to fish here with my family, and I want our village’s children to have that same chance. Asking us to race you to the last fish won’t protect anyone’s income. Your 100-ton demand offers one payday; a healthy lake offers years of them. I support Emma’s 10-ton share, with catches disclosed each month and a combined limit of 50 tons while the lake is full. But we need your agreement—not just restraint from the other four. What would it take for you to accept a fair share and leave the breeding stock intact?
